battery.title: How much charge can your battery hold today?
battery.body: Compare full charge capacity with design capacity, then check battery health, cycle count and temperature. When you plug in, the Battery tab also shows the negotiated power limit, input voltage and current.
battery.note: For a time estimate, return to Overview. It shows time to full while charging and estimates remaining runtime while discharging, even when plugged in, when enough data is available.
battery.alt: The Battery tab groups full charge capacity, battery health, cycles, temperature and adapter readings.

controls.title: Code in daylight. Let a build run with the lid closed.
controls.body: Overview brings together the desktop controls available on your Mac in the standalone app.
items: Turn on HDR boost to use the extra brightness of a compatible built-in XDR display. Switch it off indoors to conserve power.
Start your build or download, then turn on Run with Lid Closed. The background service keeps it running. Turning the switch off restores the previous sleep settings.
Expand Charge limit to choose a target. A manual power mode selection applies to both battery and external power.
controls.alt: Overview controls showing HDR boost, Run with Lid Closed, the expanded charge limit and a power mode shared by battery and external power.
controls.caption: Standalone app · Desktop controls in Overview

peak.title: Measure peak CPU and GPU power separately.
peak.body: Open Peak Power Test from the gear menu. It loads the CPU and GPU together for up to 60 seconds, samples power every half second and keeps the highest reading for each chip component.
peak.note: Available in the standalone app on Apple silicon Macs that report chip power. You can stop early. Peaks stay in the window until the next run or until you quit the app.
peak.alt: Completed test on an M2 Max showing separate peak power readings for the CPU and GPU.
peak.caption: M2 Max · Results from one 60-second run

faqs: Where can I download BatterVibe, and what does it support?

The mainland China Mac App Store currently offers version 1.0 for battery and power monitoring on macOS 13 or later. Battery details apply to MacBooks with a built-in battery. This website shows standalone 0.10.6. Store update 1.1 has been submitted to Apple.
Why is net battery power negative when plugged in?

If your Mac draws more power than it receives, the battery covers the shortfall. A positive reading means net charging and a negative one means net discharging. Input power measures DC power at the Mac’s port. The charger’s rated wattage is a separate figure.
Where can I see runtime and battery health?

Overview shows time to full when charging and estimated runtime when discharging. Estimates change with the workload. A dash means there is too little information. Open Battery for capacity, health, cycles and temperature.
How do HDR boost and closed-lid operation work?

HDR boost requires a compatible built-in XDR display. The standalone app registers its background service at launch and reconnects automatically if the connection drops. This service keeps tasks running with the lid closed. If the switch requests approval, follow its link to Login Items & Extensions in macOS and then return to the app. Switching it off restores the previous sleep settings.
How do I set a charge limit?

On a compatible Apple silicon Mac running macOS 26.4 or later, expand the standalone app’s slider and choose 80%, 85%, 90%, 95% or 100%. Store version 1.1 uses a bundled Apple shortcut. Add it on first use, then check the result in Battery settings.
Which power sources does my selected mode affect?

In the standalone app, choosing a mode updates both the battery and external power settings. High Power is available on supported models. The recent high-energy apps list requires Apple silicon and macOS 27. Its scores compare apps within that list.
How can I measure CPU and GPU power?

On an Apple silicon Mac with chip power readings, open the standalone app’s gear menu, choose Peak Power Test and click Start Test. Both components run under load for up to 60 seconds. Each peak is the highest half-second average. You can stop at any time. Sleep or severe overheating also ends the test.
How do I try, buy or restore advanced controls?

Once store version 1.1 is available, open the BatterVibe control panel from the gear menu for a 14-day free trial or a one-time purchase of CNY 6 in mainland China. The trial ends automatically and basic monitoring remains available. Choose Restore Purchases with the Apple Account used for the original purchase.

Choose Language in the gear menu to follow the system or select one of eight interface languages. The change takes effect immediately. The website’s language menu opens the same page in the language you choose.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: This policy covers battery and power readings on your Mac, local preferences, support email and Apple purchase services.
privacy.contactIntro: Contact Zhiping Jiang with a privacy question or a request to delete support correspondence.
sections: BatterVibe reads macOS battery, power and temperature information locally. Live readings are held in memory. The app keeps no battery history database and sends no readings or hardware serial numbers to the developer.
The standalone app reads CPU and GPU power and recent app energy information on your Mac. The test window keeps the current run’s peaks until you start a new test or quit the app.

Menu bar display, language and launch-at-login choices stay on the Mac. macOS may request approval for the background service used by closed-lid and power controls. The app requires no account and includes no advertising, tracking or third-party analytics.
Quitting releases live readings. Preferences remain until you remove the corresponding app data using macOS. The developer cannot access or delete this local data remotely.

Store version 1.1 uses Apple StoreKit for trials, one-time purchases and restoration. The app reads the transaction status needed to determine access. Apple handles payment information and purchase records.

If you contact support, we use your email address and message to respond and investigate. You may request deletion, subject to legal retention requirements. The website has no third-party analytics scripts. The hosting provider may process routine logs for operation and security. Apple’s privacy policy applies to App Store services.

cli.title: Read power from Terminal
cli.intro: Pass battery status, power and time estimates to a script as JSON, or change what the menu bar displays from Terminal.
cli.setup: With standalone 0.10.6 or store version 1.1 installed, set the alias below for your installation in Terminal. The first command opens the menu bar app if needed.
cli.exampleTitle: Read status and change the display
cli.limits: The standalone app also provides commands for closed-lid operation, power modes and high-energy apps. HDR and charge limits use the same hardware and access requirements as the app. For store charge limits, add the shortcut first and verify the result in Battery settings.
cli.results: Exit code 3 means the result is unconfirmed. Code 4 means the request was sent. Read the current state before repeating the command.
